cards.explanation: The answer is protect. The psalm says, "may the name of the God of Jacob protect you." Jacob is the man God renamed Israel (Genesis 32:28). The hope in that line is that this name keeps somebody safe in a hard day. I think that's a pretty good thing to have in your corner, friends.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "May He remember all your gifts and look favorably on your burnt offerings." Those two hopes ride together in the same verse, friends. Then the verse ends with "Selah."

The answer is that all of them succeed. The psalm says, "May He give you the desires of your heart and make all your plans succeed." ALL of them, friends. No plan gets left out in the hallway. That's a big hope to say out loud for somebody.

The answer is False. The hope here isn't a quiet day. The psalm says, "May we shout for joy at your victory and raise a banner in the name of our God." Shouting AND a banner, friends. I'd be loud too, and I'd probably knock my hat off.

The answer is every single request. The psalm says, "May the LORD grant all your petitions." A petition is a request, and the hope is for all of them, friends. That's the last 'may' before the psalm turns a corner.

The answer is sure. Look at the shift, friends. After all those 'mays,' the psalm says, "Now I know that the LORD saves His anointed…" Hoping turns into knowing, and you can hear it in the words. That's a solid place to stand.

The answer is name. The psalm says, "…but we trust in the name of the LORD our God." The chariots and horses are on one side, friends, and the name of the LORD is on the other. The song opened with a name too, the name of the God of Jacob.
The answer is False. The psalm says, "They collapse and fall, but we rise up and stand firm." Two groups, friends, and two very different endings. The ones trusting the name of the LORD rise up.

The answer is the king. The psalm ends, "O LORD, save the king." Then comes the line, "Answer us on the day we call." The psalm's own opening calls it a Psalm of David, friends, and the last line is a cry for the king.
